briefs.headline: Hannan beats Tug Valley 9-0 in the Region IV first round, plays at Buffalo tonight
briefs.summary: No. 7 seed Hannan's 9-0 win over No. 10 Tug Valley in the WVSSAC Class AA-A Region IV first round on Monday, Oct. 19 at Ashton is on MaxPreps as a team-reported score posted at 3:48 p.m. Tuesday, with no scorers listed; MaxPreps puts Hannan at 6-5-1 and Tug Valley at 1-5-2. The WVSSAC's boys bracket PDF, reposted Tuesday afternoon, still shows the Region IV first round unscored, and no newspaper or broadcaster this paper can read had the match. Hannan play at No. 2 seed Buffalo (11-5-1 on MaxPreps) tonight at 7 p.m. ET in the regional quarterfinal; Buffalo won the Oct. 1 regular-season meeting 5-0 at home.

briefs.headline: Rogers says Joao Pedro's hunger for goals is lifting Chelsea before Saturday's derby
briefs.summary: Joao Pedro has five goals in six Premier League matches, behind only Manchester City's Erling Haaland on eight, and Morgan Rogers told PA on Tuesday that his teammate's "hunger to score goals, his hunger to work for the team is massive." Rogers, the 117 million pound summer signing from Aston Villa, has four league goals and an assist and called Chelsea's start under Xabi Alonso "a long project" that is "going in the right direction." Chelsea, 4th, host Tottenham on Saturday at 12:30 p.m. ET and then visit Liverpool in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Wednesday, Oct. 28.

briefs.headline: Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 from two goals down as Mac Allister scores twice
briefs.summary: Georges Mikautadze scored in the fourth minute Tuesday at Anfield after Virgil van Dijk headed the ball into his path and Sergi Cardona made it 2-0 in the 29th; Alexis Mac Allister's header in the 36th and Ronald Araujo's in first-half stoppage time, both from 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha's service, levelled it, and Mac Allister tapped in Ngumoha's low cross in the 65th before Florian Wirtz added his first goal since April in the 68th. Tani Oluwaseyi pulled one back in the 87th. Ngumoha left to a standing ovation in the 74th. Liverpool are 3-0-0 on nine points, second of 36 in the league-phase table behind Paris Saint-Germain on goal difference, and host Brighton on Sunday at 10 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Maddison apologises to Coventry fans as Tottenham count the cost of Monday's win
briefs.summary: James Maddison posted on Tuesday that he had planned to kiss the Coventry badge on his first goal back after 18 months out and would "100% apologise to anyone who thought the timing was bad," the goal having come against his hometown club. Tosin Adarabioyo and Andy Robertson limped off in the first half and Omar Marmoush hobbled off in the 87th minute; Roberto De Zerbi called the injuries "nothing important" and said Conor Gallagher was fit only for the bench, with Destiny Udogie, Lucas Bergvall and Savio also absent. Dejan Kulusevski, back after 526 days, said he is "a different man, the same guy that wants to play football, but a little bit smarter." Tottenham, 16th, play at Chelsea on Saturday at 12:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Marshall beats South Alabama 20-13 on Price's late run for a first Sun Belt win
briefs.summary: Judah Price scored from 5 yards with 1:49 left Tuesday night in Huntington, finishing an eight-play, 75-yard drive after PJ Martin's 19-yard run had tied it at 13 with 4:38 to play. The teams were 6-6 at halftime on two field goals each (Jorge Diaz Nicolas from 47 and 48 yards, Davis Little from 29 and 42) before Zion Turner's 3-yard run with 3:25 left in the third gave Marshall its first lead; Turner threw for 181 yards and ran for 45, Khalil Wilkins ran for 69, and a defense that came in allowing 447.3 yards a game held South Alabama to 326 and intercepted Jared Hollins once. Marshall is 4-3 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt, South Alabama 4-3 and 2-1; the Herd are off until Oct. 31 at Old Dominion.

briefs.headline: Thunder beat Spurs 116-104 in the opener as Wembanyama goes 1 for 13
briefs.summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 points and Jared McCain 20 on 6-for-8 from three Tuesday night in San Antonio, and Oklahoma City led for all but the first five minutes in the teams' first meeting since the Spurs won Game 7 of the Western Conference finals in May. Victor Wembanyama missed his first 12 shots and finished 1 for 13 for 12 points, 13 rebounds and six blocks, a career-worst 8% from the floor; Stephon Castle scored 24 and Dylan Harper 18. De'Aaron Fox drew a flagrant foul for throwing Chet Holmgren to the floor early in the second quarter, four technicals followed, and the Thunder outscored San Antonio 31 to 16 in the period for a 65 to 44 halftime lead that a 23 to 9 Spurs run after the break could not erase. San Antonio host Houston in Austin on Friday at 9:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: 76ers beat Knicks 106-100 on ring night as James and Brown make their debuts
briefs.summary: Tyrese Maxey scored 28 points Tuesday at Madison Square Garden, Jaylen Brown had 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists in his first game since the trade from Boston, and LeBron James, starting a record 24th season, finished with 14 points, nine rebounds and six assists after the Knicks raised their championship banner. Philadelphia closed the third quarter on an 11 to 0 run and Joel Embiid answered Karl-Anthony Towns' three that had cut it to 96 to 95; Jalen Brunson scored 21 on 6-for-19 shooting and New York shot 37%.

briefs.headline: Pistons beat Celtics 121-113 after trailing by 22 as George scores 38 in his debut
briefs.summary: Javonte Green scored 19 points after sitting the entire first half and hit his fifth three for a 13-point lead with 3:33 left Tuesday in Detroit, Cade Cunningham had 22 points and eight assists and Jalen Duren 22 and nine rebounds in the season's opening game. Paul George's 38 were the most by a Celtic in a debut after Boston acquired him from Philadelphia for Jaylen Brown; Jayson Tatum, in his first full season since the 2025 Achilles tear, missed 17 of 23 shots. Boston led 72 to 50 early in the third.

briefs.headline: Hurricanes beat Canucks 6-3 to take the NHL points lead on an 11-game night
briefs.summary: Logan Stankoven and Nikolaj Ehlers each scored twice Tuesday in Vancouver for the defending champions (8-2-1), handing the Canucks an eighth straight loss. Elsewhere, Tampa Bay (7-2) won 6-2 at Vegas as Nikita Kucherov's three points pulled him level with Steven Stamkos' franchise record of 1,137; Mikko Rantanen completed a hat trick in overtime for Dallas, 3-2 over Boston, ending the Bruins' five-game winning streak; Adrian Kempe scored twice as Los Angeles won 5-2 at Washington for its first win of the season; and Macklin Celebrini's second goal, on an overtime power play, won it 4-3 for San Jose at Montreal.

briefs.headline: Ohio State plans to play the rest of the season without QB Julian Sayin
briefs.summary: Ryan Day said Tuesday that Sayin, last year's Heisman finalist, is out indefinitely with an injury to his throwing arm suffered on a fourth-quarter sack and fumble in Saturday's win at No. 5 Indiana, and that the Buckeyes are planning to go without him through the postseason. True freshman Luke Fahey, the No. 2 all season, and sophomore Tavien St. Clair will split first-team snaps during this week's bye before the Oct. 31 game at No. 19 USC; Sayin was completing 71.2% of his passes for 1,772 yards, 17 touchdowns and two interceptions.

briefs.headline: Commanders' McLaurin tears patellar tendon, out for the season
briefs.summary: Coach Dan Quinn said Tuesday that Terry McLaurin tore the patellar tendon in his left knee while cutting on a route late in the first quarter of Monday night's loss at San Francisco. The 31-year-old, Washington's leading receiver with 230 yards on 15 catches and a captain this season, signed a three-year extension in 2025 that lets the team release or restructure him after the season; he would otherwise count $34 million against the 2027 cap.

briefs.headline: NFL will not punish Eagles over Hurts playing with a blood clot, reports say
briefs.summary: The Athletic reported Tuesday, and ESPN confirmed, that the league found no violation of its injury-report policy in Philadelphia's handling of Jalen Hurts, who played the Week 5 game in London after a clot in his calf was diagnosed as superficial and is now expected to miss at least three months on blood thinners after clots were found in his lungs. The NFL said in a statement that its officials were in contact with the Eagles' medical staff and Cleveland Clinic London throughout, and chief medical officer Allen Sills called the team's approach "appropriately guarded."

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu will return at the Kyushu basho, his stablemaster says, 18 days out
briefs.summary: Tachinami oyakata (stablemaster), the former komusubi Asahoho, said Tuesday that yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu, 27, who had surgery on his right knee in late July and missed the September tournament, his third straight absence, "will come back from Kyushu," having rejoined the autumn jungyo (exhibition tour) on Oct. 10. Hoshoryu has gone 10 tournaments as yokozuna without a yusho (championship), one short of the record since 1958. The Kyushu basho (tournament) runs Nov. 8 to 22 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center, with the banzuke (rankings) due Monday; the Japan Sumo Association also announced a 15,000-seat spring exhibition at Tokyo's Ariake Arena on April 15.

prime.item: Day 7. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:44 a.m. by its files.nc.gov address (HTTP 200, PDF, pdftotext), made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The recreational limit it sets for unlicensed persons and harvesters taking oysters for personal consumption is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, seven days a week, from public bottom, with a three-inch minimum shell length; it is unlawful to take oysters between sunset and sunrise, or from the oyster sanctuaries designated in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:44 a.m. and still dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess, while its own footnote reads oyster season is Oct. 15 to March 31 unless closed earlier by proclamation, and the proclamation is the later document. The division's proclamations index, all seven pages read at 5:44 a.m., now carries two proclamations issued after FF-44-2026 of Oct. 15: FF-45-2026 and FF-46-2026, both issued Oct. 20 and effective 12:01 a.m. Oct. 28, both signed by interim director Michael S. Loeffler and both opened as PDFs (HTTP 200, pdftotext); FF-45 is the recreational snapper grouper complex order implementing Regulatory Amendment 36, a gag and black grouper aggregate vessel limit, a 13-inch, seven-per-day black sea bass rule south of Cape Hatteras and grouper seasons, superseding FF-40-2026, and FF-46 is the commercial black sea bass pot stowage order; neither names red drum, spotted seatrout, mackerel, bluefish, black drum, sheepshead, spot, flounder or oysters. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:44 a.m. with a browser user agent and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, under federal red drum management, with a footnote that it is unlawful to possess red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff them; the division's flounder proclamation FF-27-2026, which the page links and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, cites Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requiring recreational anglers to report red drum, spotted seatrout, flounder, striped bass and weakfish harvest to the division. The proclamations index, all seven pages read at 5:44 a.m., carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation; the two proclamations issued Oct. 20, FF-45-2026 and FF-46-2026, are snapper grouper complex orders effective Oct. 28 and do not name red drum. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries, and the limits page says a Coastal Recreational Fishing License is required in coastal waters under G.S. 113-174.2, a separate license from the inland one. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 20 days old, has red drum as the main inshore target around Topsail.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists spotted seatrout, the speckled trout, at a 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day, no federal regulation. The division's proclamations index, read at 5:44 a.m., lists the harvest opening as FF-31-2026, issued June 25 and effective 12:01 a.m. July 1, 2026, and carries no later seatrout proclamation; the October proclamations on the index are the oyster opening, three commercial flounder orders (FF-42, FF-43 and FF-44-2026, issued Oct. 6, 13 and 15), gill net and other gear orders (M-21 through M-24-2026, issued Oct. 2 and Oct. 9) and the two Oct. 20 snapper grouper orders, FF-45-2026 and FF-46-2026, effective Oct. 28, which do not name seatrout. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 20 days old, has the trout scattered, a few on early topwater, the guides waiting on cooler water; Beaufort's thermometer read 64.2 degrees this morning, up 0.9 from Tuesday's 63.3.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day, all under federal management plans. The two proclamations issued Oct. 20 on the division's index, FF-45-2026 and FF-46-2026, are snapper grouper complex orders and do not name mackerel or bluefish. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 20 days old, has Spanish and bluefish plentiful from the surf and piers and kings to 32 pounds at Jolly Roger Pier.

NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, with one over 25 inches allowed per person per day, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, neither under federal regulation, and spot with no minimum size and 50 per day under federal spot management. The reference calendar lists October as the peak of the spot run; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 20 days old, has black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs, spot in the evening bottom-fishing catch at Surf City Pier and sheepshead in the Seaview Pier bottom catch.

going_out.dates: Harvest Sept. 1 to 14 only; closed since Sept. 15
going_out.item: Closed. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:44 a.m., reads flounder, all species, Sept. 1 to 14 open and Sept. 15 to 30 closed, unlawful to possess, and carries no October opening; the proclamation it links, FF-27-2026, which the server delivered as a PDF (HTTP 200) and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, was signed June 3 by director Kathy B. Rawls and says it is unlawful to possess flounder for recreational purposes except from 12:01 a.m. Sept. 1 until 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14, 2026, with a 15-inch minimum and one per person per day inside that window, supersedes FF-17-2026 of March 13 and sets no later season. The division's proclamations index, all seven pages read at 5:44 a.m., now carries two proclamations issued after FF-44-2026 of Oct. 15: FF-45-2026 and FF-46-2026, both issued Oct. 20 and effective 12:01 a.m. Oct. 28, both signed by interim director Michael S. Loeffler and both opened as PDFs (HTTP 200, pdftotext); FF-45 is the recreational snapper grouper complex order implementing Regulatory Amendment 36, a gag and black grouper aggregate vessel limit, a 13-inch, seven-per-day black sea bass rule south of Cape Hatteras and grouper seasons, superseding FF-40-2026, and FF-46 is the commercial black sea bass pot stowage order; neither names red drum, spotted seatrout, mackerel, bluefish, black drum, sheepshead, spot, flounder or oysters. The three October flounder proclamations on the index, FF-42-2026 of Oct. 6, FF-43-2026 of Oct. 13 and FF-44-2026 of Oct. 15, are commercial pound net and mobile gear orders, and there is no recreational one. Flounder in Topsail Sound are release only, the 37th day of the closure; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 20 days old, has them as bycatch on red drum rigs and in the pier bottom-fishing catch.

waters.reading: 254 cfs, 2.27 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on discharge and on stage against 417 cfs and 2.72 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 254 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Down 70 on the day, still falling, the lowest the river has read since before Thursday's rise, and the recession is slowing: Tuesday's drop was 97. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, "254 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.", and the band is right: the fetcher's pushy band runs 200 to 500 cfs and the river is 54 above the 200-cfs line and 246 under the blown-out line it crossed at 4 p.m. Sunday. The 417 cfs and 2.72 feet in the fetcher's 24h_ago fields are the 5:30 a.m. Monday readings, the first points after its two-day window opens at 5 a.m., about 47.75 hours before the current reading, and the USGS 03186500 trace pulled at 5:44 a.m. puts the true 24-hour mark at 324 cfs and 2.48 feet at 5:15 a.m. Tuesday, Tuesday's edition reading, so the river is down 70 cfs and 0.21 feet on the day, not the 163 cfs and 0.45 feet the comparison implies; the falling flag is right on the day either way. The recession ran straight through Tuesday with no bump: 324 cfs at 5:15 a.m., 321 at 5:45, 317 at 6:30, 314 at 7:45, 310 at 9, 307 at 10, 303 at 11:30, 300 at noon, 297 at 2 p.m., 293 at 3:30, 290 at 4:45, 287 at 6, 283 at 6:45, 280 at 8:15, 277 at 9:15, 273 at 10:15, 270 at 11:15 p.m., 267 at 12:30 a.m., 264 at 1:15, 261 at 3, 258 at 4, and 254 at 5 and 5:15 a.m., the last point on the trace and the window low; stage went 2.48 Tuesday morning to 2.27. The rate of fall eased from about 4 cfs an hour Monday to about 3 cfs an hour Tuesday and overnight, and at that rate the 200-cfs line, where the long-leader, small-fly water begins, is about 18 hours off, longer as the recession slows, an arithmetic note and not a forecast. The window high is 421 cfs and 2.73 feet at 5 and 5:15 a.m. Monday. The Gauley near Craigsville (03189100), above Summersville Lake, read 1,060 cfs and 11.80 feet at 4:30 a.m., the last point on its trace, against 1,330 cfs and 12.05 feet at 4:30 a.m. Tuesday, the true 24-hour mark, down 270 on the day, about 10 cfs an hour. 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, its discharge series again carrying no values, an 11th day, came up Tuesday evening after 32 hours flat: 7.77 feet at 6 p.m., 8.58 at 6:15, 8.72 at 6:45, 9.07 at 7:15, 9.32 at 7:30, 9.34 at 7:45, 9.40 at 9:30 p.m., then 9.41 to 9.42 through the night, 9.41 at 4:45 a.m. today, up 1.64 feet from the 7.77 it held at 6 p.m. and still 1.62 under the 11.03 it held at 2 a.m. Monday, a reading off a USGS stage trace and not a Corps statement; the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no release figure is printed. At 254 cfs and falling the Williams is edging out of the heavy-nymph-on-the-seam problem and toward the edges-only one: the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure are fishable from the near bank and the inside seams, the middle is still not crossable, which is the fetcher's wadeable-at-the-edges line, and the water clears a little more each day on a recession this steady. Stoneflies and caddis are the forage the file records, so a weighted stonefly nymph, size 8, on point with a caddis pupa dropper, under an indicator or on a tight line, worked up the inside seams and the soft water inside each plunge pool's tail-out from the near bank, one split shot where Tuesday wanted two; sculpin are the third forage, so an olive or black weighted sculpin pattern on a sink tip swung along the undercut banks and through the plunge pools where the current drops off, and with the flow 54 cfs off the 200-cfs line, a size 14 to 16 caddis dry over the pocket water's softer seams in the afternoon is a dry-fly option again for the first time since the rise. The fetcher carries no Williams water temperature, so none is printed. WVDNR's trout stocking page was not opened today; no stocking line is printed.

waters.read: 25.4 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up 0.36 on the day after an overnight climb, and the fetcher's rising flag is right either way. The trace, pulled at 5:44 a.m., runs 25.03 at 5 a.m. Tuesday, the true 24-hour mark and Tuesday's edition reading, 25.05 at 6:15 and 7:15, then down: 24.98 at 7:45, 24.90 at 9, 24.76 at 10:45, 24.64 at noon, 24.55 at 2 p.m., 24.48 at 3:30 p.m., Tuesday's low and the window low, then up: 24.61 at 5:30, 24.77 at 6:45, 24.85 at 8, 24.97 at 9, 25.07 at 10, 25.10 at 11, 25.21 at midnight, 25.29 at 12:45 a.m., 25.31 at 2, 25.35 at 2:30, 25.40 at 3:30, 25.45 at 4:30 a.m., the window high, 25.39 at 4:45 and 25.39 at 5 a.m. That is up 0.36 on the day and 0.91 off the 3:30 p.m. low; the fetcher's 24.95 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Monday reading, not 24 hours ago, and against it the pool reads 0.44 up, so the flag holds on both counts and the day's move is outside the fetcher's 0.25-foot steady band. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.4 the gauge is in that band, 1.6 feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27 feet. What is above it is mixed: the Gauley near Craigsville read 1,060 cfs at 4:30 a.m. against 1,330 a day earlier and the Williams at Dyer went 324 to 254, both still falling, while 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, came up 1.64 feet Tuesday evening, 7.77 at 6 p.m. to 9.41 by 9:30 p.m., and has held 9.41 to 9.42 since, readings of USGS traces and not Corps statements, the Corps' Huntington District site not opened, so no lake elevation and no Corps release figure is printed; what reaches Point Pleasant and when is the Corps' call and is not predicted here. At 25.4 on a normal pool, with a 0.9-foot swing in the last 14 hours, the river fishes the structure and the current it makes: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the current breaks, the water pushed by the rise, a half-ounce blade bait or a jigging spoon on the lock wall's deep edge for the sauger, crawfish-colored jigs in the rock for the smallmouth, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark, where a rising pool moves the bait first. No West Virginia NWS product was pulled by this desk this morning.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.49 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 26.95 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.5 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Down 0.28 on the day, a third normal-pool morning, and the fetcher's falling flag is right on the day this time, by three hundredths. The trace, pulled at 5:44 a.m., runs 26.77 at 5 a.m. Tuesday, the true 24-hour mark and Tuesday's edition reading, 26.79 at 7:15 and 8:15 a.m., Tuesday's high, then down through the day: 26.71 at 9:30, 26.68 at noon, 26.59 at 1 p.m., 26.52 at 3, 26.40 at 3:30, 26.23 at 5, 26.14 at 6:30, 26.06 at 8:45, 26.02 at 9:15 p.m., Tuesday's low and the window low, then up: 26.11 at 10, 26.13 at 11:30, 26.21 at 12:15 a.m., 26.26 at 1:45, 26.30 at 2:15, 26.37 at 3, 26.40 at 3:45, 26.44 at 4:30, 26.48 at 4:45 and 26.49 at 5 a.m. That is down 0.28 on the day, just outside the fetcher's own 0.25-foot steady band, and up 0.47 off the 9:15 p.m. low; the fetcher's 26.95 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Monday reading, not 24 hours ago, and against it the gauge reads 0.46 down, so the flag holds on both counts. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 26.5 the gauge is 0.51 under the 27-foot line between that band and up and pushing, where it spent Saturday and Sunday; the window high is 26.96 at 6:15 a.m. Monday. The overnight climb here, 0.47 since 9:15 p.m., runs with Point Pleasant's 0.91 since 3:30 p.m. upstream. What is above is mixed: the Gauley near Craigsville 1,060 cfs at 4:30 a.m. against 1,330 a day earlier, the Williams at Dyer 324 to 254, both falling; 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, up 1.64 feet Tuesday evening to 9.41 by 9:30 p.m. and holding 9.41 to 9.42 since, readings of USGS traces and not Corps statements. The Craigsville water is above Summersville Lake, which sits between it and this gauge; what the lake passes is the Corps' call and is not predicted here. At 26.5 and moving a half-foot inside the day, the third normal-pool morning after four days up and pushing, the fish are on the structure and not the slack: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam rather than the eddy behind it, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head along the riprap points in low light, a black-and-blue jig for the smallmouth and the drum in the rock, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark; the lock wall fishes from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids when the gates open. No West Virginia NWS product was pulled by this desk this morning.

Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 4:10 AM at 3.9 ft, low 10:07 AM at 1.1 ft, high 4:31 PM at 4.5 ft, low 10:46 PM at 0.9 ft. waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 4:41 AM and 5:12 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Three days past the quarter and five from the full: the fetcher's file carries the moon as waxing gibbous, 77 percent lit and 10.0 days old, and the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered at 5:44 a.m., puts the first quarter at 16:12 UT Oct. 18, the full moon at 04:12 UT Oct. 26, 12:12 a.m. ET next Monday, and the last quarter at 20:28 UT Nov. 1, so the swings grow each day this week toward the spring tides, harder current through the inlet and more bait moving on the tide; today's sound range is 3.0 feet on the afternoon flood against Tuesday's 2.9, and the evening ebb drains 3.1 feet to the day's lower low, 0.8 at 11:40 p.m. NWS Wilmington has one product on the water this morning and nothing on the beach at Topsail. The Small Craft Advisory for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles (AMZ250, also AMZ252), the marine zone off the beach and the inlet, was reissued at 1:44 a.m. today: seas 4 to 6 feet until 6 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 21, conditions the Service calls hazardous to small craft, a marine product for the ocean out 20 miles and not a sound product; the seas are down from Tuesday's 4 to 7 feet, the 15-to-25-knot north wind line that ran in Tuesday's version is gone from the text, and the end time held at 6 p.m. Wednesday. Coastal Pender (NCZ106), the Topsail zone, carried no active product at 5:44 a.m., a second morning; the next county south, Coastal New Hanover (NCZ108), has a Beach Hazards Statement from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. today, issued 5:17 a.m., a strong north-to-south longshore current mainly in the morning and a moderate rip current risk, which stops at the county line and is not printed as Topsail's. All four sound events fall inside Wednesday this morning and none carries a spillover tag: the sound at Hampstead topped out at 3.4 feet at 4:41 a.m., is on its ebb at press time, draining 2.5 feet to a 0.9-foot low at 11:05 a.m., then fills 3.0 feet to a 3.9-foot high at 5:12 p.m. and drains 3.1 feet to a 0.8-foot low at 11:40 p.m.; sunset is 6:29 p.m. and sunrise 7:21 a.m. ET at Topsail from the sunrise-sunset.org API, not the fetcher, so the last two and a half hours of the evening ebb, about 9 to 11:40 p.m., run in the dark. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: high 4:10 a.m. at 3.9, low 10:07 a.m. at 1.1, high 4:31 p.m. at 4.5 and low 10:46 p.m. at 0.9, a 3.4-foot flood and a 3.6-foot ebb against Tuesday's 3.2 and 3.3. Today's lags from the two tables are 31 and 41 minutes on the highs and 58 and 54 minutes on the lows; the lows again lag longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 64.2 degrees at 5:30 a.m., up 0.9 from Tuesday's 63.3, the first rise after three mornings of falling, and still 12.8 under Saturday's 77.0, the earlier figures cited from the week's editions; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is 20 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:44 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings showing more at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered over the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, trout scattered on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, trout quiet until the water cools, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jr. topwaters and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs on shrimp; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp soft plastics under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under feeding birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait thick, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem: the sound is on its morning ebb until 11:05 a.m., 56 minutes later than Tuesday's, and the last two hours of it, about 9 to 11:05 a.m., are the red drum stage and fall in full daylight, finger mullet the forage the file records and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low; the report's first-hour topwater for trout, a Spook Jr. walked over the deeper grass edges, falls on the top half of the ebb this morning, 7:21 to about 8:30. The flood from 11:05 a.m. to 5:12 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges, mud minnows and shrimp the forage there, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they go under, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead, the report's three- to four-pounders. The 5:12 p.m. high puts 3.9 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 3:15 to 5:12 p.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts, with sunset at 6:29 an hour and a quarter into it. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the evening ebb, roughly 9:30 to 11:40 p.m., 47 minutes later than Tuesday's and in the dark, the same Carolina-rigged mullet and cut mullet at the channel edges; Beaufort's thermometer has stopped falling for a morning at 64.2, so the cool-down the guides in the report say the trout are waiting on is on the gauge but not yet steady, and a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes, 15 to 20 feet, on the first of the evening ebb, then the dock lights after the 11:40 p.m. low, is the trout program the report describes. Oysters are in their seventh day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. The surf side is under the Small Craft Advisory's 4 to 6 feet of sea on the water out 20 miles through 6 p.m., with no beach product at Topsail today; the piers' Gotcha-plug Spanish bite on the flood to the 4:31 p.m. high, 4.5 feet at the pier, and the evening cut-bait session for slot reds fall inside it. Slack at 11:05 a.m., 5:12 p.m. and 11:40 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only, the 37th day.
